headline: PLS.AX rockets nearly 10% today while gold hits $4,215 — your portfolio's biggest day in a while.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a cracking session today, jumping nearly 10% to $6.52. No specific news in today's feed, but the move suggests a strong catalyst — likely a lithium price bounce or sector re-rating news. Worth checking ASX announcements directly if you haven't already.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI had a solid day today, up nearly 3% to $17.41. The AI theme continues to attract buyers — this ETF holds global AI-exposed companies, and positive sentiment from last night's US tech session is flowing through. Still below your buy-in price of ~$19, but heading in the right direction.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG closed up 1.33% today at $76.20, riding a strong ASX session (the ASX 200 was up nearly 2%). As a broadly diversified fund, it benefits when both local and global markets are running hot — and both were today.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS closed up 1.22% at $519.67 today. This ETF mirrors the US total share market, and it's benefiting from last night's positive S&P 500 session (up 0.5%) combined with the Aussie dollar holding steady around 70.5 US cents.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up 0.46% to $91.32 today. Emerging markets had a quieter session but still caught some of the global risk-on mood. No specific catalyst in today's data.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG nudged up 0.45% to $358.16 in last night's US session — a quiet but positive move. No big news driving it, just steady buying in the broader tech space alongside a positive S&P and NASDAQ session.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT was basically flat last night, up just 0.1% to $390.74. Still sitting below your average buy-in price (down about 12% overall). No fresh catalysts in today's data — the stock is in a holding pattern.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO dipped slightly last night, down 0.16% to $211.75 — essentially flat. No specific news. The stock is still down about 8.7% from your entry. Keep an eye on any GTA VI release date updates or earnings commentary as the next likely catalyst.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 1.03% today to $8.63, weighed down by a sharp drop in crude oil last night — WTI oil fell 3.23% to $84.88 a barrel. When the oil price drops, energy company shares typically follow, so no surprise FUEL had a rough session. Still marginally in the green overall (+2% on your investment).

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals (PLS.AX) — nearly 10% surge today
watch_today.detail: PLS jumped $0.58 to $6.52 today — a near-10% move in a single session. That's a big, sharp move and no news article came through explaining it. Before you do anything, check the ASX announcements page for PLS to see if there's a company update, lithium price move, or broker upgrade driving this. If it's fundamental, it could have legs. If it's just sector noise, it may give some back.

watch_today.title: Gold surging to $4,215 — a safe-haven signal worth watching
watch_today.detail: Gold jumped 3.05% last night to $4,215 USD per ounce — that's a very large single-session move for gold. Gold typically spikes when investors are nervous about something (inflation, geopolitical tension, recession fears). It's worth keeping an eye on what's spooking markets, as it could flow through to risk assets like your growth ETFs and tech stocks.

watch_today.title: Oil dropped 3.2% last night — FUEL.AX feeling the pinch
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) fell from $87.71 to $84.88 last night — a 3.2% drop in one session. That's the main reason FUEL.AX slipped 1% today. If oil keeps falling (whether from weak demand signals or OPEC supply decisions), FUEL could remain under pressure this week. Your overall position is still slightly positive (+2%), so no panic needed — but watch it.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — bouncing back but still below buy-in
watch_today.detail: GXAI had its best session in a while today, up 2.96% to $17.41. That's encouraging, but you're still down about 8.5% on this position (paid around $19 average). The AI theme remains strong globally and last night's US tech session was positive. If you believe in the long-term AI story, this looks like a hold — no strong reason to add or sell right now.

watch_today.title: ASX 200 surged nearly 2% today — broad-based rally
watch_today.detail: The ASX 200 closed at 8,804 today, up 1.98% — a very strong session across the board. This lifted most of your ASX holdings (VDHG, VTS, VGE, GXAI all up). With the S&P 500 also positive last night, global sentiment is clearly in 'risk-on' mode right now. Good tailwind for your growth-heavy portfolio.

watch_today.title: MSFT still underwater — patience required
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is your biggest dollar loss position — down about $47 AUD (nearly 12%) from what you paid. Last night it was essentially flat (+0.1%). There's no fresh negative catalyst, but no recovery catalyst either. This is a hold situation: Microsoft's AI business (Copilot, Azure) is growing strongly, but the market hasn't fully rewarded it yet. Don't sell into weakness unless your thesis has changed.

markets.summary: A big day all round. The ASX 200 closed up nearly 2% at 8,804 — one of the stronger sessions of the year. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 gained 0.5% and the NASDAQ crept up 0.31%, so US tech was quietly positive. The standout macro move was gold, which jumped over 3% to $4,215 USD an ounce — a signal that some investors are getting nervous and parking money in safe assets. Oil, on the other hand, fell over 3% to $84.88 a barrel, which dragged on energy stocks. The Aussie dollar was dead flat at 70.49 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Strong local session — one of the best days of the year for the Aussie market.

indicators.note: Last night's US session was modestly positive. Markets holding near highs.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech was a little quieter than the broader market last night, but still in the green.

indicators.name: Gold (USD/oz)
indicators.note: A sharp 3% jump — gold is surging as investors seek safety. Worth watching what's driving nervousness.

indicators.name: Crude Oil WTI (USD/bbl)
indicators.note: Oil dropped hard last night — bad news for energy stocks like FUEL.AX.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar barely moved — essentially flat at 70.5 US cents.

sport.summary: Round 15 is wrapping up — a big week for Queensland teams. The Dolphins demolished the Roosters 48-10 at Suncorp on Friday night, and there's a cracker of a local derby still live: Wests Tigers vs Titans tied 28-28 in the second half right now.

stories.title: Dolphins 48 def. Roosters 10 — Suncorp Statement
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins put on a clinic at Suncorp Stadium on Friday night, hammering the Roosters 48-10. That's a 38-point margin — an absolute flogging. The Dolphins are in red-hot form and looking like genuine finals contenders heading into the back half of the season.

stories.title: Rabbitohs 48 def. Broncos 6 — Accor Thumping
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney put 48 points on the Broncos on Thursday night at Accor Stadium, winning 48-6. The Broncos will have some serious soul-searching to do after being outclassed so heavily. A very disappointing result for a side that fancies itself as a contender.

stories.title: Sharks edge Warriors 10-8 in Auckland
stories.why_it_matters: The Cronulla Sharks ground out a tight 10-8 win over the Warriors at Go Media Stadium in Auckland on Saturday afternoon. A close, grind-it-out game — the Warriors will be frustrated to lose at home by just two points.

stories.title: Titans vs Wests Tigers — 28-all at half-time, still live!
stories.why_it_matters: The Gold Coast Titans are locked at 28-28 with the Wests Tigers at Leichhardt Oval and it's in the second half right now. If you're a Titans fan, get the stream up — this one's going down to the wire.

stories.title: Eels hold off Raiders 15-12 at CommBank
stories.why_it_matters: Parramatta got the job done at home on Saturday night, beating the Raiders 15-12 in a tight contest at CommBank Stadium. Not a vintage performance from the Eels, but two competition points is two competition points.
